publishedWalks.title: Lady’s Beautiful Highgate Walk and Map — A Lady in London
stops: Highgate High Street and Pond Square
themes: Residential architecture, independent businesses, greenery and views
A longer neighbourhood exploration rather than a one-hour station loop
stories: Primarily a sightseeing itinerary, not a collection of detailed historical anecdotes; cemetery admission and swimming are optional diversions. Advertises 2–3 hours. Locator: route and walk-details sections, lines 26–95. Source family: independent travel blog; September 2022 URL, revision date unknown. ([aladyinlondon.com](https://www.aladyinlondon.com/2022/09/highgate-walk.html))

publishedWalks.title: The Highgate Village Self-Guided Walk — Richard Jones
stops: Highgate West Hill and Holly Lodge Estate
stories: Advertises two hours. Relates fictional David Copperfield settings, Coleridge’s residence and reburial, and the reservoir’s role in piped water. Fictional-location identifications are qualified, not established biography. Locator: lines 51–149. Source family: commercial walking-guide author; publication and revision dates unknown. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

publishedWalks.title: Highgate Village: Tales of History and Mystery — The Highgate Society / VoiceMap
stops: Highgate Cemetery western entrance: advertised start
The Flask: publicly available preview stop
stories: The public Flask preview distinguishes the earlier establishment from the later building and recounts Turpin and ghost legends; these are advertised tales, not verified events. The producer also describes resisting high-street road widening. Advertises 2 km, 60 minutes and 42 locations, not a Highgate station loop. Only public listing and preview material inspected; full stop inventory unavailable. Locators: lines 87–132, 175–185 and 233–277. Source family: local society-authored commercial audio tour; publication date unknown. ([voicemap.me](https://voicemap.me/tour/london/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery))

publishedWalks.title: Ring 2 Walk 3: Highgate walk to West Hampstead — trainwalkslondon
stories: Discusses Waterlow’s estate gift, a mansion fire, garden-suburb housing, water-supply ponds and Kenwood’s collecting history. These remain guide claims requiring independent historical verification before narration. Advertised distance: 5.4 miles. Locators: lines 18–110 and 173–184. Source family: independent walking blog; published February 16, 2025. Outside the proposed loop’s practical scope as a complete itinerary. ([trainwalkslondon.wordpress.com](https://trainwalkslondon.wordpress.com/2025/02/16/ring-2-walk-3-highgate-walk-to-west-hampstead/))

candidates.name: Waterlow Park: public landscape and civic gift
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: how private grounds became a shared amenity. The Friends identify Waterlow’s gift and an 1891 opening, with ponds and hillside views. Present anchor: a public park path overlooking the landscape, exact standing point unselected. Locator: The Park, lines 35–43; community stewardship source, undated. Gate times require verification. ([waterlowpark.org.uk](https://www.waterlowpark.org.uk/the-park/))

candidates.name: Lauderdale House exterior
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: a house understood through its surrounding public landscape, rather than an interior visit. Present anchor: an exterior park path, subject to gate access. The operator locates it within Waterlow Park and describes a steep station approach; architectural and social-history propositions remain to research. Locator: How to find us, lines 16–37; operator source, undated. ([lauderdalehouse.org.uk](https://www.lauderdalehouse.org.uk/plan-your-visit/how-find-us))

candidates.name: Pond Square: a name outlasting water
candidates.why: Investigate the guide’s filled-pond claim through the present square; distinguish documented landscape change from folklore. Proposed anchor: public square, position unverified. Guide locator: line 84. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Highgate Literary and Scientific Institution exterior
candidates.why: Investigate neighbourhood learning beyond celebrity residents. Proposed anchor: public pavement facing 11 South Grove, not its interior archive. Guide locator: lines 93–97. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Reservoir beside The Grove
candidates.why: Investigate water infrastructure behind the picturesque village. Proposed anchor: public passage beside the mound; visibility and access unverified. Guide locator: lines 114–118. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: 3 The Grove: Coleridge and the Gillman household
candidates.why: Investigate care and domestic literary life, avoiding romanticised addiction. Proposed anchor: public pavement facing the residence and reported plaque. Guide locator: lines 122–124; private property excluded. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: St Michael’s Church exterior
candidates.why: Investigate parish formation and changing commemoration. Proposed anchor: public South Grove pavement; no reliance on courtyard access or seeing an interior grave. Guide locator: lines 100–104. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: The Flask exterior: buildings versus pub legends
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: separating a pub’s physical chronology from stories attached to it. The public audio preview itself treats Turpin as a tale; ghost accounts must remain folklore. Proposed anchor: opposite public pavement, not customer seating. Locator: preview location 36, lines 175–185; local society/commercial tour source, undated. ([voicemap.me](https://voicemap.me/tour/london/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery))

candidates.name: Highgate Cemetery western entrance, exterior only
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: interpreting the cemetery boundary rather than promising access to famous graves. The Society’s published tour explicitly starts outside this entrance. Proposed anchor: Swain’s Lane public pavement away from the entrance flow; standing space unverified. Locator: lines 275–278. Historical claims need cemetery-source research; this candidate may cost too much loop time. ([voicemap.me](https://voicemap.me/tour/london/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery))

candidates.name: Highgate Wood edge: landscape alternative
candidates.why: Alternative to the southern cemetery extension, not an assumed addition. The published blog routes walkers from the station into the wood. Proposed discovery: investigate woodland management rather than repeat picturesque descriptions. Proposed anchor: a verified public entrance/path; historical evidence and exact gate remain unresolved. Locator: route lines 28–35; independent travel blog. ([aladyinlondon.com](https://www.aladyinlondon.com/2022/09/highgate-walk.html))
